question: When should you give a signal before turning or changing lanes?
options: In good time before you make the move
Only when another car is behind you
Only at night or in rain
explain: Rule 103: To give clear signals in good time.

question: What should you do with your indicator after completing a turn?
options: Make sure it cancels straight away
explain: Rule 103: To cancel your signal after finishing the turn so it does not mislead.

question: If you signal early, does that give you the right to pull out?
options: Yes, other drivers must stop for you
No, you must still wait until it is safe
Yes, if you signal for three seconds
explain: Highway Code Rule 103 reminds drivers that signals show intent and never give priority.

question: Why could a late signal confuse other road users?
options: It gives them too little time to react safely
It breaks the speed limit rule
It turns off your brake lights
explain: Highway Code Rule 103 stresses signalling early enough for others to read and react.

question: Who needs to see your signal before you turn?
options: Other drivers, cyclists, and pedestrians nearby
explain: Rule 103: Signals warn all road users of your plans.

question: When should you avoid giving a signal?
options: When it could confuse or mislead other road users
explain: Rule 103: Not to give misleading signals.

question: What should you do before signalling to pull over and stop?
options: Check your mirrors to see who is behind you
explain: Highway Code Rule 103 works with mirror checks so others understand your signal.

question: If you want to turn into a side road just past a parked car. When do you signal left?
options: After passing the parked car so nobody thinks you are stopping
explain: Rule 103: Early signals near parked cars can mislead others.

question: If your indicator bulb fails before a drive, what should you do?
options: Fix it before driving, or use clear arm signals if safe
Use hazard lights for every turn
explain: Highway Code Rule 103 includes arm signals when indicators are not working.

question: When pulling away from the side of the road, when should you signal?
options: Before you pull away, if other road users could benefit
explain: Rule 103: Signalling in good time when pulling away.

question: Why should you check that your indicator has cancelled after a gentle bend?
options: Self-cancelling switches may not turn off after a small steer
It is required only on motorways
Indicators turn off after two flashes
explain: Highway Code Rule 103 reminds you to cancel signals manually if they stay on.

question: Two side roads are close together on your left and you want the second one. When should you signal?
options: As you pass the first side road
100 metres before the first side road
After turning into the second road
explain: Rule 103: Not to signal before an earlier turning you are not taking.

question: A driver behind flashes their lights after you signal left. What does your signal give you?
options: No right of way; wait until the move is safe
explain: Rule 103: Signals never give you priority over anyone else.

question: What should you check before cancelling a signal early if you change your mind?
options: That nobody has already reacted to your first signal
explain: Highway Code Rule 103 stresses clear, unambiguous signals at all times.
